### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| "+N months" computation | Every effect via cumulative re-run of `shocks.runway` on lever-adjusted (income, spending, buffer, oneOff) | The judge formula is the single source of truth; a shortcut formula (e.g. `buffer/gap` deltas) can drift at the `no_shortfall`/cap branches | Direct formula on gap | One runway call per lever step; trivial cost (integer math, <1 ms budget) |
| Lever sizing base | Levers sized from **profile** numbers (S, F, P, insurance), never shocked ones | Judge hand-checks use part-1 metrics; shock additions (bills +15%, extra monthly) are not discretionary and must not be "cut away" by a lever | Size against shocked spending | Under a bills shock the trim lever cannot absorb the increase; that is the honest answer |
| Discretionary margin | `disc = max(0, S − (F + P))` with `trim_discretionary` spending down exactly to the F+P cut floor | Matches the E2-approved cut floor definition; zero when no margin exists (explicit "no margin" row) | Percent-of-spending cuts (arbitrary) | Accounts with tiny margins (68257: disc = $9.19) show +0.0 months; that is a true finding, not a bug |
| Levers below the floor | `defer_loan` (−P) and `shop_insurance` (−insurance) deliberately go under F+P and are labeled as structural moves ("simulated counterfactual") | Deferral is real bank hardship practice with P exact in the data; insurance renegotiation is bounded by `insurance_cents` | Forbidding all floor breaches (would kill 2 of 3 levers) | The printed floor line must say "ordinary cuts stop at F+P; labeled structural moves go under it on purpose" |
| Standing-orders lever | **REJECT** | `standing_orders.csv` is not in `profiles.json`; adding it means an E1 schema change (exact-key loader, verify.py, frozen fixtures) and the source is an undated snapshot | Precompute per-account order sums in E1 | Lever set misses "cancel discretionary standing orders"; acceptable, recorded in decisions |
| Secondary-buffer lever | **REJECT** | No cross-account linkage exists (transfers land at partner banks outside the dataset); `balance_series` is the same single account's money | "Restore buffer to 12-month peak" (not a lever the customer can pull) | `buffer_depleted` accounts show all levers at +0.0; surfaced as an honest plan line instead |
| Goal target | Keep `3 × S` starter with `6 × S` stretch chips (GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6 = the EI duration) | Standard emergency-fund guidance is 3 to 6 months of spending; the challenge's own twist runs 6 months at 55%, so 3 is starter and 6 is storm-ready; both printed as "our definition" | 6 × S only (less reachable; weakens the goal story) or 3–6 range formula (two headline numbers) | A judge preferring 6 × S sees it as the stretch chip row |
| Months to target | Keep scaffold `ceil(target / contribution)` from zero (EXTEND verdict; keeps E2 invariant) + printed "savings on hand" disclosure line | Changing it breaks the approved E2 plan numbers and the invariant in the test plan | Netting B into months (see Q1) | Two facts on the card (months from zero, buffer on hand) instead of one netted number |
| Python twin | **RESTORE, test-side only** (no build.py/verify.py coupling) | Data Use rubric (25%) rewards "every plan number cross-checked by two independent implementations against frozen goldens"; cross-language drift is the recurring failure mode and `golden_fixtures.json` parity is the established remedy; drafts already exist so cost is ~150 lines | Abandon + delete (zero cost, loses the drift guard and the rubric argument) | Every future plan rule change needs two edits; a missed edit is a failing pytest, which is the point. Time-boxed fallback: abandon if the TS side slips (Q2) |
| Golden fixture file | New frozen `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` (do not touch `golden_fixtures.json`) | `golden_fixtures.json` is frozen E1 hand computation; plans need their own frozen table with workings | Extend `golden_fixtures.json` | One more fixture file; matches the established pattern |
| ConsoleView/store | Zero changes; `buildPlanText` composes planMath internally | The one seam (`plan={derivation.plan}`) survives E3's concurrent mount work untouched; no merge conflicts | ConsoleView computes planMath in its useMemo and passes parts down | `buildPlanText` is a slightly larger composer; acceptable since it is already the "arithmetic lives here" layer |

### Interfaces

All money fields integer cents; all month counts integers; sentinels `MONTHS_UNREACHABLE = -1`, `CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE = -1` (existing).

```ts
// src/lib/planMath.ts (new)

/** The 6 month stretch cushion, the EI duration in the challenge twist. */
export const GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6            // sits beside GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3
export const GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6] as const

export interface GoalMilestone {
  monthsOfSpending: number        // k in "k months of typical spending"
  amountCents: number             // k x S, integer cents
  monthsToReach: number           // ceil(k x S / contribution), or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  isGoal: boolean                 // k === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS
  isStretch: boolean              // k === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS
}
export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[]

export type LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'

/** One lever's explicit effect on the shocked cash flow, integer cents. */
export interface LeverEffect {
  incomeDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever
  spendingDeltaCents: number      // <= 0: every E4 lever cuts monthly spending
  bufferDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever (no data backed buffer lever)
}

export interface Lever {
  id: LeverId
  label: string                   // plain words, the ladder row title
  caveat: string                  // honesty tag, "simulated counterfactual, ..." (dash clean)
  effect: LeverEffect
}

export interface LeverInputs {
  // Shocked numbers, straight from ShockResult (never re-derived here).
  shockedIncomeCents: number
  shockedSpendingCents: number
  oneOffCents: number
  bufferCents: number             // profile.buffer_cents (pre one-off), for the re-run
  // Profile numbers the levers are sized from (judge part-1 metrics).
  fixedCostsCents: number         // F
  loanPaymentCents: number        // P (0 when no running loan)
  insuranceCents: number          // median insurance
  typicalSpendingCents: number    // S
}

export interface LeverStep {
  lever: Lever
  incomeAfterCents: number        // cumulative, integer cents
  spendingAfterCents: number      // cumulative, integer cents
  bufferLeftCents: number         // bufferCents - oneOffCents (unchanged by E4 levers)
  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer       // shocks.runway re-run from scratch after this step
  plusDeciMonths: number          // cumulative vs shocked baseline, tenths, >= 0
  stepDeciMonths: number          // marginal vs previous step, tenths, >= 0
}

export interface LeverLadder {
  baseline: RunwayAnswer          // the shocked runway each step improves on
  steps: LeverStep[]              // application order, only levers the data supports
}
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder
```

**Lever semantics (the contract table):**

| Order | id | Availability | Effect (integer cents) | Honesty label (caveat) | Floor interaction |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `shop_insurance` | `insuranceCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −insuranceCents` | "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation" | Goes under F+P on purpose (premium itself is renegotiated) |
| 2 | `trim_discretionary` | `disc = max(0, S − (F+P)) > 0` | `spendingDelta = −disc` | "simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed" | Lands exactly on F+P |
| 3 | `defer_loan` | `loanPaymentCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −loanPaymentCents` | "simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled" | Goes under F+P on purpose (P itself is deferred) |

Composition rule: `leverLadder` filters to available levers in order 1→2→3, applies effects **cumulatively** (`spendingAfter = max(0, shockedSpending + Σ deltas)`; the `max(0, ...)` is a defensive guard, asserted unreachable on all fixtures), and re-runs `shocks.runway(bufferCents, oneOffCents, shockedIncome, spendingAfter)` per step. Display rules for the +N column (in planText, dash clean): both finite → `"+X.X months"`; baseline finite and after `no_shortfall` → `"clears the shortfall (120+ months)"`; baseline `buffer_depleted` → `"+0.0 months (buffer depleted: restore a positive balance first)"`.

```ts

  label: string          // "1 month of spending" ... "6 months of spending (stretch)"
  amountCents: number
  monthsToReach: number  // or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  highlight: 'goal' | 'stretch' | 'plain'
}

export interface LeverRow {
  id: LeverId
  label: string
  caveat: string
  effectCents: number            // magnitude of the monthly spending cut
  runwayAfter: string            // formatDeciMonths(runwayAfter.deciMonths, state)
  plusLabel: string              // per display rules above
  plusDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
  stepDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
}

export interface PlanText {
  goal: string[]          // E2 lines + cut/status lines (numbers from goalPlan)
  goalChips: GoalChip[]   // milestone chips, goal block
  backup: string[]        // E2 lines + cut floor / horizon definition lines
  levers: LeverRow[]      // the ladder table rows
  definitions: string[]   // the "our definition" disclosure strip
}
// signature unchanged:
export function buildPlanText(profile, result, twist, band): PlanText

E6 judge mode and E7 Solana touch next. ## Product A financial resilience engine for real bank customers, built for the Tangerine track of the Sheridan Datathon 2026. At judging a judge picks an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five minutes: 1. **Know the customer.** Any account shows typical income I, fixed costs F, spending S, savings buffer B, household bills H, loan payment P, gap, and months of runway, all from the precomputed profile artifact. 2. **Take a shock.** A shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up 15 percent, a one-off repair, or a mix) changes income or spending and the runway recomputes with the judge's branch rules. 3. **Make a plan.** A goal plan (emergency fund) and a backup plan (if the shock lands) built from the same numbers. The one-minute pitch opens with the Storm Atlas: the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts, then one click drills into any account for the live twist. Every number a judge sees traces back to source rows through provenance checksums. The orbit game and the findings-first report framing are dropped as surfaces; their machinery may be reused internally. ## Hard constraints - **Judge definitions are the contract.** I, F, S, B, H, P and the runway come from docs/tangerine-challenge.md. Any deviation must be deliberate, documented in docs/decisions.md, and explainable to a judge. - **Integer cents end to end.** Dollars convert with `np.rint(dollars * 100)` once at load; every metric, mean, median and runway division afterwards is integer arithmetic with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero). No float may decide a branch. - **Deterministic offline artifact.** profiles.json carries no timestamps, no randomness, and no floats; two consecutive builds are byte identical. All data is bundled for an offline booth. - **Checksummed sources fail loud.** The three canonical CSVs are verified against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before any row is read. - **Any account must work.** All 4500 accounts, including the five edge flags (pensioner, thin history, zero income, defaulted loan, negative buffer), must render without a special case. - **One weather vocabulary.** src/lib/verdict.ts owns the five bands (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) over integer deci months (10, 30, 60, 120).
